subject: Recap: dedicated capacity sizing & deployment preference (Cerebra Health)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Gardner <tom.gardner@cerebrahealth.com>, ops@cerebrahealth.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-02T15:12:00Z
Subject: Recap: dedicated capacity sizing & deployment preference (Cerebra Health)

Hi Tom / Ops team —

Thanks again for an excellent discussion today. Quick recap and the actions we discussed so we keep momentum on the sizing and deployment decision: 

Summary from call:
- Primary use: clinical note summarization + search reranking for patient queries (P1).
- Preferred deployment: leaning toward Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) with an option to move to Private VPC later for PHI-sensitive workloads.
- Primary constraints: predictable latency (<300ms p95 for 256-token outputs), HIPAA controls, and fixed monthly cost window for FY27 planning.

Sizing inputs we need from you (items you said you'd confirm):
1) TPS targets (steady / peak) — you mentioned ~50 steady TPS with spiky peaks to ~220 TPS during morning intake. Please confirm.
2) Token mix: average request size and generation length. We heard 350 input tokens avg, 220 output tokens avg; is that correct for your 85% summarization traffic and 15% rerank/embedding calls?
3) KV-cache locality: do you expect long conversation chains (session affinity) vs mostly stateless requests?
4) Acceptable latency SLO and whether you prefer cost-optimized batching vs strict single-token latency.

Engineering note: based on the call I asked Aditya to draft two preliminary SKU options (A100 80GB baseline vs H100 80GB for aggressive concurrency). We'll attach a draft capacity worksheet for you to review.

Next steps (agreed):
- Tom: confirm TPS steady/peak and token mix by EOD Wednesday (2026-11-04).
- Ops/procure: share any MSA/PO timing constraints and whether you'd require private deployment in the kickoff.
- Redwood: provide a formal Dedicated capacity estimate + cost delta for H100 vs A100 and an optional Private VPC addendum. Deliverable ETA: 48 business hours after your confirmations.

Attachments: cerebra-capacity-draft.xlsx (attachment), redwood-dedicated-options.pdf (attachment).

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0189
From: Tom Gardner <tom.gardner@cerebrahealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@cerebrahealth.com, procure-team@cerebrahealth.com
Date: 2026-11-03T09:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Recap: dedicated capacity sizing & deployment preference (Cerebra Health)

Neha —

Appreciate the recap and the clear next steps. Confirming numbers below so you can proceed with the estimate: 

- Steady TPS: 45 requests/sec (this is what we see across the clinic app midday).
- Peak TPS: 210 requests/sec (30–45min windows during patient onboarding).
- Token mix: our telemetry today shows median input ~320 tokens, median output ~200 tokens. Overall traffic: ~82% summarization, ~12% reranking, ~6% embeddings (background).
- Conversation patterns: mostly stateless single-turn summarization for ingestion pipelines; session affinity is low except for a small pilot (approx 5% of traffic).
- Latency: track to p95 < 300ms for the summarization path. Rerank can tolerate up to 800ms in exchange for lower cost.

On deployment: we want Dedicated now for isolation and predictable billing, and then evaluate Private VPC in Q2 2027 for archived PHI workload segregation. That means API keys stay in Redwood but we will likely add VPC later.

Procurement note: we need a draft quote for our procurement team (PO timeline is ~4 weeks). Please include the H100 vs A100 line items and monthly committed throughput tiers.

Thanks — Tom
Tom Gardner
VP Product, Cerebra Health
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Gardner <tom.gardner@cerebrahealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-03T15:46:00Z
Subject: Re: Recap: dedicated capacity sizing & deployment preference (Cerebra Health)

Thanks Tom — helpful numbers. Two quick clarifying questions from an engineering perspective so the SKU mix is accurate: 

1) Token distribution tail: can you share 90th percentile input/output token sizes if possible? That helps size KV cache and memory headroom (we're conservative for HVY tails).
2) Reranking pattern: are the 12% rerank requests short-window batched jobs (e.g., 16 items per batch) or individual low-latency calls? If batched, what typical batch size?

Preliminary recommendation (subject to your p90 numbers):
- If p90 token lengths are within 1.5x medians, A100 80GB x16 would likely meet steady + peak with autoscale headroom (cost-efficient).
- If p90 is > 1.5x and you need consistent p95 latency, H100 80GB x12 with higher concurrency and aggressive KV caching will be safer.

We can also propose a hybrid: baseline A100 capacity for 24/7 steady load and a burst H100 pool for morning peaks (automated routing). That option increases ops complexity but gives a good cost/latency tradeoff.

If you can share the p90 token files (or a small sample log), I can run a quick simulation and attach a refined capacity worksheet.

— Aditya
Lead Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Tom / team —

Perfect — thanks for confirming. Quick plan from Redwood:

1) We'll run a simulation on your p50/p90 numbers if you can share a one-day sample (anonymized) — Aditya will take that and return a simulated TPS profile plus two SKU proposals (A100-focused and H100-focused) within 48 business hours.
2) I'll produce a formal quote (MSA/line-item) that includes: committed baseline, burst H100 hourly option, and an optional Private VPC addendum (timed Q2 2027).
3) Tentative POC kickoff: week of 2026-11-22 assuming procurement runs to plan. If PO needs to align sooner, flag it and we can provide a short-term starter bundle on hosted API for first 2–4 weeks.

Action items: 
- Tom: share anonymized token-size log (S3 link or CSV) — target: by EOD tomorrow (2026-11-05).
- Procure: confirm PO window and if a purchase order number will be used (we'll draft quote accordingly).

I'll attach the baseline worksheet and a short one-pager on the hybrid burst option so procurement and engineering have clear tradeoffs.

Best,
Neha
